actions.title: Fix tsconfig.json's include path so the build gate actually runs

pr.title: Fix tsconfig.json include path (finding #1)
pr.body_summary: Implements analysis.json finding #1. include was ["todo-app/src"] inside a config that already lives in todo-app/, resolving to todo-app/todo-app/src and matching nothing - tsc exited TS18003 in 10 of 11 sessions in harness-logs/. Changed to ["src"]. Verified by re-running npm run build.

actions.rationale: Direct, checkable fix against the exact file the finding cites - no judgment call about which of two legitimate options to pick.

actions.title: Pick one formatting enforcement mechanism

options.label: A: Adopt a formatter
options.change: Approve adding prettier as a dev dependency (the exact thing rejected mid-session in b6205fd8), add a `format` script, and rewrite the style guidance in CLAUDE.md/AGENT.md/style-consistency to point at it instead of 'match the surrounding file'.
options.tradeoffs: Removes the judgment call entirely. Costs a new dependency and a small amount of build-tooling churn - why this needs a human sign-off, not a silent implementation.

options.label: B: Codify one explicit rule, no new dependency
options.change: Replace 'match the surrounding file's conventions' in both CLAUDE.md and AGENT.md with one explicit, stated rule (e.g. 'always single quotes'), and update style-consistency's SKILL.md to reference the same rule.
options.tradeoffs: Zero new dependencies. Depends on every future session actually reading and following the text rule - f95c8207/b6205fd8 already show this codebase's style drifting twice under text-only guidance.

actions.rationale: Adding a dependency vs. relying on text-only guidance is a call this data doesn't settle. Implementing either silently would be guessing on the team's behalf.

actions.title: Resolve the commit and plan-approval contradiction between CLAUDE.md and AGENT.md

options.label: A: AGENT.md wins on autonomy
options.change: Delete CLAUDE.md's 'commit once a piece of work is in a reasonable state' and 'run with it rather than stopping to wait for a go-ahead' lines. Agent never auto-commits, always stops after a plan for explicit approval.
options.tradeoffs: Matches what actually happened in e6041b83 - a human had to reject an autonomous commit the agent made following CLAUDE.md's wording. Slower iteration.

options.label: B: CLAUDE.md wins on autonomy
options.change: Delete AGENT.md's 'do not commit changes automatically' and 'wait for them to say go' lines. Agent commits as work reaches a reasonable state and runs with plans without waiting.
options.tradeoffs: Faster iteration. But the only real evidence in this dataset (e6041b83) is a human actively blocking exactly this behavior.

actions.rationale: Both files are internally consistent on their own; the conflict is between them, and nothing in the input files states which one the team wants. A values call, not a bug an agent can implement its way out of.

actions.title: Fix the broken SKILLS.md reference
actions.diff:
--- /dev/null
+++ b/todo-app/SKILLS.md
@@ -0,0 +1,9 @@
+# Skills
+
+- **code-formatter** — Use for formatting and style nits in this repo — spacing, quote style, import order, small naming tweaks. Scope is src/.
+- **plan-and-ship** — Use when someone asks for a plan, approach, or design for a change in this repo.
+- **refactor-cleanup** — For when a piece of code has grown messy and needs a proper cleanup pass — extra abstraction, duplicated logic, confusing structure. Most relevant in src/state, src/features, and src/components.
+- **style-consistency** — The codebase mixes naming conventions and folder depth across files (camelCase, kebab-case, PascalCase, inconsistent nesting). Use this to bring a file or folder in line with the convention used elsewhere.

pr.title: Add missing SKILLS.md (finding #3, mechanical part)
pr.body_summary: CLAUDE.md references SKILLS.md twice but it doesn't exist. Every name/summary here already exists in harness-snapshot.json's skills array, so this is assembly, not judgment - implemented directly. The policy half of finding #3 (autonomy contradiction) is a separate, flagged action; this PR doesn't touch that.

actions.rationale: Nothing here requires inventing content or making a judgment call, only assembling what harness-snapshot.json already has.

actions.title: Remove the two dead hooks unrelated to the commit-policy question

pr.title: Remove two dead hook registrations (finding #4)
pr.body_summary: pre-read-format-check.js and prompt-plan-reminder.js are both loc_active: 0 while registered live in settings.json. Removed the dead registrations. post-edit-autocommit.js is intentionally not touched here - see action 6, blocked on the still-open policy decision in action 3.

actions.rationale: Both hooks are loc_active: 0 while registered live - a verifiable fact. Removing the dead registration (rather than guessing at restoring hook bodies neither analysis.json nor the transcripts specify) is the safer of two equally-mechanical options.

actions.title: post-edit-autocommit.js: do not implement yet
actions.rationale: This hook's entire purpose - maintaining a running auto-commit trail - is the exact behavior AGENT.md forbids and CLAUDE.md invites, i.e. action #3. Reviving it presumes option B there; deleting its registration presumes option A. Implementing either now would silently decide action #3 on the team's behalf. Wait for #3 to resolve, then this becomes mechanical.

actions.title: Determine the team's actual target shell/OS before writing anything into the guides
actions.harness_component: todo-app/CLAUDE.md and todo-app/AGENT.md (neither states an OS/shell)
actions.next_step: Ask the team, or check for an authoritative source outside these files (CI config, a devcontainer/.tool-versions file, package.json engines/os fields) - don't infer an answer from these transcripts. The transcripts themselves are inconsistent: 7c3e9b15/b6205fd8/48a7d3c1 show a Unix `head` call failing with a PowerShell-style error, and in 48a7d3c1 the very next attempt (`Get-Content`, real PowerShell syntax) fails too, this time with a bash-style error - contradictory evidence about which shell is actually in play. Writing a guessed answer into CLAUDE.md would just replace one wrong assumption (the agent's) with another (this skill's).
